We need to answer the question: "Our IT lead is setting up SSO for the first time and asked me to check whether a login loop back to the sign-in page usually means the redirect URL is misconfigured."

We have policy excerpts that say: "A sign-in that returns to the login page immediately after the identity provider approves it is almost always a redirect URL mismatch rather than a credentials problem." So answer: yes, it's usually a redirect URL mismatch. Provide guidance: check callback URL matches reply URL exactly, trailing slash, http/https mismatch, etc. Provide steps: copy callback URL, compare, re-save. So we can answer.

We must not mention policy or instructions. Just answer. Use short and specific. So we will post reply.

function.arguments: {"message":"Yes – a loop that sends you back to the sign‑in page right after the identity provider approves the login is almost always caused by a redirect URL mismatch. Check that the callback URL shown in Settings → Security → SSO → Configuration matches the reply URL (or redirect URI) you’ve set up on the identity provider side exactly – including the trailing slash and http/https scheme. If there’s any difference, update the provider’s configuration and re‑save it, then try signing in again."}
